from.place: Proof opening: Choose a compactification c=(j,p); the local compact-support-extension and cofiltered-coherent-diagram splits require coherent comparisons of this choice. This is an agent-added foundation, not a WANTED quotation from the blueprint.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $y$ of $Y$ and write $X_y=\{y\}\times_YX$. A horn in $X_y$ gives a lifting square for $p$ with bottom the constant simplex at $y$; a lift remains over $y$. Hence $X_y$ is Kan, even though $X,Y$ need not be Kan. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], $|p|$ is a Serre fibration. Apply the current finite-limit clause of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] to the degreewise pullback $X_y=\Delta^0\times_YX$, where $\Delta^0\to Y$ selects $y$. It gives the canonical homeomorphism $|X_y|\cong\{ |y|\}\times_{|Y|}^{\mathcal K}|X|$. The same statement specifies that limits in $\mathcal K$ are k-ifications of topological limits. Therefore this is exactly the fiber of $|p|$ with the k-space fiber topology required below; no ordinary-product topology or Kan condition on $Y$ is substituted. Thus the exact sequence, path lifting and component action of [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] apply to this fiber.

source.place: Corollary 3.6.2 and Theorem 3.6.4; Lemma 2.4.16; agent explicit horn pullback argument.

proof.text: Assume $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Surjectivity on realized components supplies a point $x\in|X|$ and a path from $|p|(x)$ to $|y|$. Lift this path using [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence]; its endpoint lies in $|X_y|$, so that fiber is nonempty. Fix any $e\in|X_y|$. The orbit set of $\pi_1(|Y|,|y|)$ on $\pi_0(|X_y|)$ is the set of components of $|X|$ mapping to the component of $|y|$, which is a singleton because $\pi_0(|p|)$ is bijective. The stabilizer of the component of $e$ is the image of $\pi_1(|X|,e)$; this image is the whole group because $|p|$ induces an isomorphism. The action is therefore both transitive and fixes that component, so $\pi_0(|X_y|)$ is a singleton. This is the required connectedness, without assuming either total space or base connected.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.16 and Proposition 2.4.18, low-degree component/path-lifting argument; agent orbit/stabilizer expansion.

proof.text: For each $e\in|X_y|$ and $n\geq1$, use the exact segment $\pi_{n+1}(|X|,e)\to\pi_{n+1}(|Y|,|y|)\to\pi_n(|X_y|,e)\to\pi_n(|X|,e)\to\pi_n(|Y|,|y|)$ from [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence]. The first map is surjective, so the connecting map is zero and the map out of $\pi_n(|X_y|,e)$ is injective. The last map is injective, so that injective map has zero image. Hence $\pi_n(|X_y|,e)=0$. Together with step 2 and the Kan assertion of step 1, this proves that every vertex fiber is a contractible Kan complex in the precise weak-contractibility convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 3.6.4, fiber argument, with Lemma 2.4.16; explicit kernel/image calculation.

proof.text: Assume all vertex fibers are contractible Kan. For any such fiber $K$, apply [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] to $K\to\Delta^0$ with target $K$. Precomposition $U:K\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,K)$ has a simplicial homotopy inverse $V$. Evaluate the homotopy $UV\simeq\mathrm{id}$ at $\mathrm{id}_K$ and transpose: this gives $J:K\times\Delta^1\to K$ between the constant map at $k=V(\mathrm{id}_K)$ and $\mathrm{id}_K$. For $n\geq1$ and $a:\partial\Delta^n\to K$, restriction of $J$ along $a$ gives an edge between the constant boundary map at $k$ and $a$. By [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map], applied to $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and $K\to\Delta^0$, restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,K)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^n,K)$ is Kan. Its dimension-one horn lifting lifts this edge from the constant simplex at $k$; the other endpoint fills $a$. Either orientation of $J$ works since both one-dimensional horns lift. For $n=0$, weak contractibility gives $|K|\ne\varnothing$; a simplex representing a realization point has a vertex, which fills the empty boundary. Thus every map $\partial\Delta^n\to K$ extends to $\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq0$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.17; explicit evaluation at the identity and dimension-one lifting through the restriction fibration (Kerodon 00TM; Mathlib PushoutProduct.lean:70-93).

proof.text: Given a boundary square $a:\partial\Delta^n\to X$, $\sigma:\Delta^n\to Y$ for $p$, put $T=\Delta^n\times_YX$ and $q:T\to\Delta^n$. Pairing any horn lift for $p$ with its specified simplex coordinate proves that $q$ is Kan. The map $a$ gives a section $a'$ over $\partial\Delta^n$. Its fiber over $0$ is $K=X_{\sigma(0)}$. The monotone function $c(j,0)=0$, $c(j,1)=j$ on $[n]\times[1]$ induces a simplicial contraction of $\Delta^n$ from the constant map at $0$ to the identity. Step 4 gives the extension property $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^n,K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta^n,K)$ required by [lem-cbc-kan-contracted-base-section-extension]. Apply that lemma with $L=\Delta^n$, $C=\partial\Delta^n$, $E=T$: the resulting section extends $a'$, and its projection to $X$ fills the original square. This also applies at $n=0$, with empty boundary. Therefore $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration as defined in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. No Kan hypothesis on $T$ or $Y$ was used.

source.place: Agent application of the extracted contracted-base section-extension lemma to the monotone simplex contraction; preserves the original step-4 route.

proof.text: If $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration, [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] supplies $g:Y\to X$ with $pg=1_Y$ and a simplicial homotopy from $1_X$ to $gp$. The identity homotopy on $Y$ supplies the other composite. Applying [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to these maps proves that $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Steps 1-6 give the three-way equivalence for arbitrary Kan fibrations, including non-Kan bases.

source.place: Lemma 08NS, lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy, lines 5641-5664; Kerodon Proposition 3.1.7.13 (00UB) for realization weak equivalence.

proof.text: Let $B$ be Kan. Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] to $i:\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and to $B\to\Delta^0$. The first map is degreewise injective, and the second is a Kan fibration by the definition of Kan complex in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The target corner pullback is $\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^1,B)$: both functor spaces into $\Delta^0$ are the one-point simplicial set. Since $\partial\Delta^1=\{0\}\amalg\{1\}$, restriction to it is the pair of endpoint evaluations, and its functor space is degreewise $B\times B$. Thus the joint endpoint map $q:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\to B\times B$ is a Kan fibration.

source.place: SSet.fibration_pullbackObjObjπ, lines 70-72; terminal-target specialization at 144-148. Explicit degreewise identification with joint endpoint restriction.

proof.text: For $f:A\to B$ with $A,B$ Kan, the map $P(f)\to A\times B$, $(a,\gamma)\mapsto(a,\gamma(1))$, is the pullback of $q$ from step 7 along $(a,b)\mapsto(f(a),b)$. A horn square for this pullback is solved by the lift for $q$ together with its prescribed $(a,b)$ coordinate. The projection $A\times B\to B$ lifts horns by filling their $A$ coordinate in the Kan complex $A$. Given a horn square for their composite, first fill in $A\times B$ and then lift to $P(f)$. Thus the stated endpoint map $p_f:P(f)\to B$ is a Kan fibration. Since $B$ is Kan, filling a horn first in $B$ and then lifting shows that $P(f)$ is Kan too.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10, second bullet; elementary pullback/projection/composition lifting argument, using the joint endpoint result established in step 6.

proof.text: Let $r:P(f)\to A$ forget the path and $i:A\to P(f)$ assign the constant path at $f(a)$. Then $ri=1_A$. The order-preserving function $\min:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ induces a simplicial map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$. Precomposing each path with $s\mapsto\min(s,t)$ defines $H:P(f)\times\Delta^1\to P(f)$, $H((a,\gamma),t)=(a,\gamma(\min(-,t)))$. This formula means the exponential transpose, so it defines all simplex degrees and commutes with all simplicial operators. It remains in $P(f)$ because $\min(0,t)=0$. At $t=0$ it is $ir$; at $t=1$ it is the identity. Thus $i,r$ are simplicial homotopy inverses. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], $i$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10, first bullet; agent explicit min-contraction in place of invoking the endpoint trivial-fibration theorem.

proof.text: The equality $p_fi=f$ holds since the final endpoint of the constant path at $f(a)$ is $f(a)$. The two-out-of-three property of weak homotopy equivalences of k-spaces in [lem-coef-topological-serre-model], applied to the continuous maps $|i|$, $|p_f|$ and $|f|$ between realizations (all objects lie in $\mathcal K$ by the current realization-values clause of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]), and step 9 show that $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $p_f$ is. Apply the three-way criterion of steps 1-6 to the Kan fibration $p_f$. Its strict fiber over $b$ is degreewise exactly $A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B}\{b\}$, the homotopy fiber in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence exactly when every homotopy fiber is contractible. If $B$ is empty, existence of $f$ forces $A$ and $P(f)$ empty and all conclusions remain valid; otherwise an empty fiber fails contractibility because its component set is empty.

source.place: Remark 3.4.0.6, using the explicitly constructed factorization and the already proved criterion; Hovey Theorem 2.4.23 for topological two-out-of-three.

title: Contractible fibers and trivial Kan fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalence, Kan complexes and contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A Kan fibration means a simplicial map lifting every horn inclusion, and a trivial Kan fibration means a map lifting every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq0$. For a Kan fibration $p:X\to Y$, the following are equivalent: $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence; $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration; every vertex fiber is a contractible Kan complex. For a map $f:A\to B$ of Kan complexes, the mapping-path replacement $P(f)=A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_1}B$ is a Kan fibration; the constant-path map $A\to P(f)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Consequently $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if all its homotopy fibers are contractible. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ denotes the union of the faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.7.6 (00ZP). The mapping-path replacement uses the endpoint path-space fibration of Theorem 3.1.3.1 and the interval contraction; its vertex fibers are the homotopy fibers defined in def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones. The mapping-path part is an agent-specified expansion, not a quotation of another numbered construction.
